To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) estrogen-alpha, progesterone and androgen receptor positivity were associated with clinicopathological features of the tumor and the women with ovarian cancer; and (2) there was no significant contribution of the steroid receptor, HER2 or the triple-negative status to disease-free or overall survival of the women with epithelial carcinoma of the ovary.
the steroid receptor status and the HER2/neu status of women with epithelioid ovarian cancer are not related to their disease-free and overall survivals.

(a) estrogen-alpha staining was associated positively with disease-free survival, (b) progesterone receptor staining in women with a BMI ≥25 and (c) androgen receptor staining in serous tumors were associated with steroid receptor expression, and (d) there was no association between steroid receptor, HER2 status or TNEOC with disease-free or overall survival.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the contribution of steroid receptors including estrogen-alpha, estrogen- beta, androgen receptor and progesterone receptor status, HER2 status and TNEOC status to disease-free survival in women with primary epithelia ovarian cancer.
the contribution of immunological steroid receptor and HER 2 expression to survival in women with ovarian cancer.
the association between the steroid receptors and the HER2 expression status with survival of patients with epithelial ovarian carcinoma.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
steroid receptor expression, the HER2 and triple-negative status do not seem to be of prognostic significance in epithelial ovarian cancer.
there is no association between immunohistochemically detectable steroid receptor, HER2 status and the TNEOC status and survival in this cohort of women with epithelium ovarian cancer.
the contribution of the steroid receptors to survival of women with ovarian cancer is not significant.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

although steroid receptor and the HER-2 status are important markers for the diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment of epithelial ovarian cancer, their contribution to survival in women with primary epithelium ovarian cancer is not significant.
steroid receptors, HER2 and TNEOC status are not associated with survival in epithelial ovarian cancer.
the contribution of immunological detection of steroid receptor and the HER 2 status to survival is not as strong as it has been previously reported.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the triple-negative status does not appear to confer worse prognosis to patients with ovarian cancer.
the triple-negative phenotype is not associated with a poor prognosis in epithelial ovarian cancer.
the immunohistochemical status of steroid receptor, HER2 status or TNEOC is not a significant prognostic factor in women with epitheloid ovarian cancer.
